title: H2O: Human-to-Humanoid Teleoperation Depends on Closed-Loop Data Filtering
content_lines: Source: [arXiv:2403.04436v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.04436v1). Code claims are tied to the pinned official human2humanoid revision linked by the Chinese page.

> **Bottom line:** H2O first aligns human motion to H1, trains a privileged full-body tracker, uses that tracker to reject motions the simulated robot cannot follow, and then trains a policy robust to real visual and hardware errors. The reusable mechanism is robot-in-the-loop data curation, not direct camera-to-joint copying.
## Engineering problem

Monocular human pose contains scale ambiguity, occlusion, jitter, and motions outside the robot's morphology or balance envelope. Training on every retargeted sequence rewards the policy for targets that are impossible or unsafe.
## Method

The pipeline performs shape-aware human-to-robot retargeting, privileged imitation learning, simulation rollout filtering, and robust deployment training. Closed-loop success of the target robot becomes a dataset label, so feasibility is measured through the controller rather than inferred only from pose distance.
## Key figures
![Figure 4: complete H2O pipeline](../assets/h2o-2403.04436/figure-4-pipeline.jpg)
Figure 4 makes the sim-to-data filtering loop explicit between retargeting and final policy training.
![Tables I-II: rewards and randomization](../assets/h2o-2403.04436/table-1-2-training.jpg)
The tables locate the tracking objective and sim-to-real perturbations instead of treating robustness as an unspecified training trick.
![Tables III-IV: filtering and scale](../assets/h2o-2403.04436/table-3-4-filtering.jpg)
The comparisons show that unfiltered motion and dataset scale do not have the same effect: more data helps only after feasibility control.
## Decisive evidence

The filtering ablation is decisive because it changes data acceptance while keeping the overall policy family comparable. It supports the claim that target-robot trackability is a first-class data-quality signal.
## Paper-to-implementation mapping

The pinned repository provides retargeting/tracking environments, reward and termination logic, motion loading, and hardware deployment paths. Audit those interfaces together: a training policy without the same preprocessing and feasibility filter is not an equivalent H2O reproduction.
## Limits and evidence boundary

Visual pose estimation and robot state estimation still constrain latency and robustness. The filter is policy-dependent and can reject motions that a stronger future controller could learn. Reported H1 deployment does not certify other morphologies or contact-rich manipulation.
## Bounded engineering takeaway

Store a feasibility score and rejection reason for every retargeted clip. Re-run the filter when the robot model, low-level control, simulator, or tracking policy changes; do not treat accepted data as permanently valid.
## Reproduction checklist

Lock human-pose input, shape alignment, robot model, retargeting, teacher policy, termination thresholds, filter version, final-policy randomization, and hardware rate. Report accepted/rejected counts, tracking error, fall/contact failures, visual latency, and real interventions.
